newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Treas says privatization funds to pay debt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Treas says privatization funds to pay debt.

text.p: The head of Brazil's National Treasury said Tuesday privatization receipts had always been assigned to debt retirement under previously stated government policy.
"We don't need a new decree for that," Eduardo Guimaraes told reporters. "Money from privatizations will be used to retire debt."
Guimaraes was responding to confusion generated among local media by a decree published Tuesday which sought to allow state firms to use old untradeable privatization credits to pay off debt.
Under Brazil's National Privatization Program, privatization funds have automatically been earmarked for debt.

But that tradition was broken with the sell-off earlier this year of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), when half of the proceeds from the sale of a controlling stake was ploughed into a special fund for infrastructure investment.
The debate over how to use privatization receipts heated up Tuesday when Communications Minister Sergio Motta called for the money to be used for social projects and economic development.
